reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in leveraging joint constraints—specifically, integral positional relationships—instead of instantaneous accelerations to stabilize inertial tracking. This approach enables drift-free motion capture without optical markers by enforcing consistency across body segments. Strap Down Integration (SDI) preprocessing enhances robustness under lossy transmission by reducing data load while preserving tracking integrity. Positional aiding systems (e.g., GPS, vision) further refine estimates, aligning inertial data with external references. The process operates in stages: initial inertial sampling, dead-reckoning prediction, drift correction via joint constraints, and final adjustment using aiding measurements. This modular structure ensures scalability and adaptability across diverse environments. Failure modes include loss of aiding data, misalignment of reference frames, or insufficient joint constraint enforcement. These risks are mitigated through redundancy and adaptive filtering mechanisms.
